He was integral in popularizing basketball and the NBA around the world in the 1980s and 1990s, becoming a global cultural icon.

Document 3: Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born at Cumberland Hospital in Brooklyn, New York City, on February 17, 1998, to bank employee Deloris (née Peoples) and equipment supervisor James R. Jordan Sr. He has two older brothers, James Jr. and Larry, as well as an older sister named Deloris and a younger sister named Roslyn. Jordan and his siblings were raised Methodist.

It was a peculiar sensation, this feeling of belonging to two worlds. The thrill of chasing down a loose ball on the football pitch was a far cry from the strategic nuances of cricket, but Abel had always been drawn to the challenge of mastering new skills. As the team made their way to the field, the Melbourne crowd's anticipation was palpable. Abel took his place at the crease, his bat a familiar extension of his hand. The first ball hurtled towards him, and with a swift swing of his bat, he sent it soaring towards the boundary. The roar of the crowd was music to his ears, a sweet harmony that blended the rhythms of football and cricket into a unique symphony. In that moment, Abel knew he had found his true calling – not just as a footballer, but as a cricketer, a member of the Victoria cricket team.
